To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the yield of photoelectrons from a medium with two-photon ionization is small in the case of a small cross section of the intermediate transition and that the energy cost of photoionizing such a medium is small in the self-induced transparency regime.

the photoionization of a medium by a laser pulse with two-photons excitation of an inter-mediate level is a process that is characterized by an extremum in the ionization efficiency as a function of photo-ionization cross section.
the ionization yield for photoionization of a weakly absorbing medium by a laser pulse with two-step excitation of an excited state has a maximum at an optimum value of the absorption cross section.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fundamental processes that occur when intense ultrashort laser pulses interact with matter.

the development of the theory of the interaction of ultrashort laser pulses with matter, the development of new methods of laser diagnostics of the properties of matter, and the development of new laser methods for the modification of the properties of solids.
the development and use of laser spectroscopic techniques in the study of the interaction of intense laser radiation with matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ionization of a medium by a laser pulse is possible in the case where the two-photon transition is induced by the field of the laser pulse and where there is no two-photon self- induced transparency.
the two-photons self-induced transparency for an ultrashort pulse is an effective method for the efficient and inexpensive production of a laser-plasma.
the two-photonic ionization is not the best choice for the ionization process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionizing laser pulse is an effective tool for the coherent control of the ionization process in a medium.
the two-photons self-induced transparency is a powerful tool for controlling laser-plasma interaction.

the photoionization of a weakly ionized medium by an ultrashhort laser pulse with a two-photon excitaion of an intermediate level is a process that can be described by a two-photon selfinduced transparency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionization yield is a non-monotonic function of the photoionization cross section.
a coherent two-photonic ionization of a gas is possible in the field of a laser pulse with an intensity of 10^{14}-10^{15} W/cm^{2}.
the yield of electrons in photoionization of a medium by a strong laser pulse can be significantly lower than in the case of the one-photon transition.
